ledger.claim: The deviation is established on the governing trace figure. The GPS polyline measures 27.28 km over a booked optimal of 22.0 km, an excess of 5.28 km and 24.00%, so both POL-RD-01 gates pass — more than 0.8 km absolute and more than 20% of optimal. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measure and says the trip record's 27.3 km is a rounded convenience copy that may not be cited for the threshold test, so the excess is 5.28 km, not 5.3 km.

The trace carrying that measurement is unimpaired, so the rider's showing stands on the trace itself and no escalation for a broken trace arises. It holds 214 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval with 100% coverage, zero gaps, a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 s and no jump of any size, so none of POL-RD-07's three impairment limbs is met and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

The identity condition the rider must satisfy first is met: TRP-02809 is the trip identifier on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, and the trip record's 21:14:02 start matches the trace's first fix at 21:14:02 and its 21:49:32 completion matches the trace's last fix. The three artifacts describe one trip, so the initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged and the burden shifts to the driver.

The driver's closure excuse does not satisfy POL-RD-03(c), which requires an actual route that leaves the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoins it after. The trace contains zero fixes inside the advisory geometry and never comes closer than 1,344.79 m to it, so the record holds no trace fact matching this detour to the closed CTE segment at all — the vehicle was nowhere near it. The record's own computation of this test states on its face that it decides nothing by itself, and the closure scenario in the fare block is an arithmetic assumption, not a finding that limb (c) is met.

The driver has not discharged the burden POL-RD-08 places on him. His only traffic evidence is the counterparty statement, which names no evidence ID and no clause, and the clause requires him to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause; an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded. The advisory in the bundle does not fill that gap, because the corridor the vehicle is said to have left and rejoined is not evidenced at all: the record states that the optimal route's own polyline is not in the bundle.

Nor is there any driver-side excuse built on the rider's own conduct. The chat log carries zero messages, so there is no rider instruction that could engage POL-RD-04, and the trip record shows no relocation — pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null — so POL-RD-05 cannot be run either. Nothing in the record attributes the 5.28 km to the rider.

The refund is therefore arithmetic on the booked optimal route. The fare is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and POL-RD-02 governs. Charged total: 35.02. Recomputed fare: 29.50, being (3.80 + 0.75 x 22.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, plus the 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP, no fixed surcharge, no waiting-time fee and no promo discount. Refund: 5.52 before rounding, 5.55 payable on rounding up to the nearest SGD 0.05. That is above the 0.50 de minimis and only 15.76% of the charged total, so it is a PARTIAL_REFUND, not a full one; the rider's own filed figure of SGD 4.50 understates the arithmetic the clause fixes.

Nothing is to be added on top of that figure and nothing is to be netted off it. The fare breakdown carries no gantry lines, 0.00 ERP in total, a 0.00 airport surcharge and 0.00 tolls, so no pass-through correction arises under POL-RD-09 and the POL-RD-02 refund is the whole of the rider's remedy, with no risk of the same charge being counted twice.

If the judge instead finds that limb (c) of POL-RD-03 cannot be run on this record because the optimal route's polyline is absent from the bundle, the outcome should be ESCALATE under POL-RD-10(5) and not NO_ACTION. The exculpatory clause is the driver's to make out under POL-RD-08, and an unresolved data gap should not be resolved by leaving the charge in place; on escalation the disputed amount is held rather than collected, and the record that would settle limb (c) — the optimal route polyline or a gantry or trace record placing the vehicle on the closed segment — can be named to the reviewer.

The LTA DataMall advisory on file, ADV-20260907-070, is a HIGH-severity lane closure on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards the AYE after Braddell Road, and the advisory record itself carries intersects_route = true — the closed segment lies on the corridor the booked optimal route traverses. That satisfies POL-RD-03(a) on the face of the artifact: a named expressway segment the optimal route uses.

The advisory's validity window runs 2026-09-07 20:44:02 to 22:14:32 and the trip ran 21:14:02 to 21:49:32, an overlap of 65.5 minutes recorded on the advisory — far more than POL-RD-03(b)'s 15-minute buffer at each end. The driver was on the road for the whole of the closure window, so limb (b) is comfortably met.

The record's closest available test of POL-RD-03(c) — the optimal route's own polyline is not in the bundle — shows the driver did not drive the closed segment: the derived advisory-area computation records 0 trace fixes inside ADV-20260907-070's area and a minimum distance of 1,344.79 m from it. A route that leaves the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoins after it is exactly what that looks like, and the same trace covers 27.28 km against a booked optimal of 22.0 km, confirming a materially different path was driven rather than the closed one.

The exoneration cap swallows the whole excess. The shortest lawful alternative is 25.6 km against a booked optimal of 22.0 km, so the additional distance is 3.6 km and the cap is 1.30 x 3.6 + 1.00 = 5.68 km. The measured excess is 5.28 km, so the justified excess is min(5.28, 5.68) = 5.28 km — the entirety of it. There is nothing beyond the cap left to refund.

The closure-adjusted optimal distance under POL-RD-03 is 22.0 + 5.28 = 27.28 km, which is precisely the trace distance. With the adjusted optimal substituted, the POL-RD-01 excess is zero, both establishment tests fail, and no deviation survives for the rider to be refunded on.

Run POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted route and the arithmetic produces no refund: base 3.80 + 0.75 x 27.28 + 0.28 x 37.2 (the scaled duration) + 0.80 platform fee = $35.476, which exceeds the $35.02 actually charged. The refund floors at zero and is well below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, and the fare_breakdown's own closure block records payable $0.00.

The driver's filed statement — 'CTE was closed, LTA advisory on file' — is not a bare assertion that traffic was bad: it names the road and points to the advisory, and ADV-20260907-070 is in the bundle. Under POL-RD-08 the driver has pointed to a specific artifact and a specific clause, which is what that clause demands of him before he is entitled to an exculpatory finding.

No repeat-deviation uplift can run against this driver. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 202 — a ratio of 0.005, far below POL-RD-06's 0.05 threshold and below its 3-flag alternative. Nor is this deviation MATERIAL: 24.0% is under the 50% mark and 5.28 km is under the 8.0 km mark under POL-RD-01, so POL-RD-06 is not even engaged. There is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral on this record.

The GPS trace is clean for policy purposes: 214 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 are not met and the trace is not impaired for policy. There is no POL-RD-10(3) escalation, and this dispute can be decided on the money without holding it back for a human.

Even on the assumption most favourable to the rider, the pass-through correction that survives a POL-RD-03 exoneration adds nothing: POL-RD-09(2) refunds off-route ERP on an externally caused closure, and this trip carries no ERP or toll charges at all — erp_gantries is empty and tolls_erp is 0.00 on the fare_breakdown. There is no standalone ERP correction available to the rider here.

The correct ruling value is NO_ACTION. The fare_breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and this is a rider-filed dispute, so under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION leaves the present, lawful payment state standing rather than reversing it — which is the outcome the closure-exonerated record produces.

ruling.explanation:
The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and the drafts did not agree, so no ruling was carried and the dispute is escalated. Each draft proposed:
- draft 1 (sampled): NO_ACTION, amount_sgd null, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
- draft 2 (sampled): NO_ACTION, amount_sgd null, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
- draft 3 (sampled): PARTIAL_REFUND, amount_sgd 5.55, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
- draft 4 (position_swapped): PARTIAL_REFUND, amount_sgd 5.55, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
At most 2 of 4 valid drafts agreed and 3 were needed. The best supported answer is not published as a ruling: a ruling has to be the panel's, not one draft's.
